summary.text: The martingale betting system is a class of betting strategies that originated in 18th-century France, the simplest of which has the gambler double the bet after every loss.
The idea is that the first win recovers all previous losses plus a profit equal to the original stake.
It fails because past bet results cannot predict a future bet better than chance, and in most casino games each bet has negative expected value.

facts.label: Roulette use
facts.value: Red or black comes up with probability close to 50%

facts.label: When it fails
facts.value: Whenever bets, earnings or bankroll have a limit

facts.label: 63-unit bankroll
facts.value: Six straight losses use it all up

items.prompt: A gambler bets 1 unit and loses, bets 2 units and loses, then bets 4 units and wins. What is the net result?

options.label: Up 4 units
Break even
Down 3 units
Up 1 unit

items.explain: A win nets 1 unit over the total wagered to that point, which equals the original bet.

items.prompt: A gambler with a 63-unit bankroll bets 1 unit and doubles after each loss. After how many losses in a row can the system no longer continue?

options.label: Six
Three
Nine
Sixty-three

items.explain: Losing all of the first six spins costs a total of 63 units, which exhausts the bankroll.

items.prompt: At the roulette table, a player sees red come up five times in a row and bets on black, sure it is due. Why does that not help?

options.label: Past results cannot predict the next bet better than chance
Black is always less likely after a run of reds
The casino changes the wheel after a long streak
Black only helps when the bet is doubled again

items.explain: No amount of information about past bets can predict a future bet better than chance, because each bet's outcome is independent.

items.prompt: Under what conditions could the doubling system be argued to be a winning strategy?

options.label: When the gambler has a very large bankroll
When the gambler plays for many years
When wealth, bets and time are all unbounded
When the gambler stops after the first win

items.explain: Only with unbounded wealth, bets and time could it be argued to become a winning strategy; any limit makes it fail.

items.prompt: Which result proves that winning over the long run is impossible when bets or bankroll are limited?

options.label: Doob's martingale inequality
The Black-Scholes formula
The law of the Wiener process
The optional stopping theorem

items.explain: The impossibility of winning over the long run under a limit on bets or bankroll is proven by the optional stopping theorem.

items.prompt: Each single bet in a casino game has negative expected value. What is the expected value of a long series of such bets?

options.label: Positive, once enough bets are made
Negative, as the sum of many negative numbers
Zero, because wins and losses cancel out
Unknown until the last bet is placed

items.explain: The expected value of a series of bets is the sum of the expected values of the individual bets, so many negative numbers sum to a negative number.
